newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker in light trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker in light trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker in quiet trade on Monday, amid profit-taking, a lack of significant economic data, and concern about tomorrow's public testimony by Alan Greenspan, analysts said.

"It's profit-taking from the huge rally we've had the last little while. The profit-taking started last Thursday so technically the market is in a corrective phase at the moment," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed-income research with Midland Walwyn Capital Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.24 to C$118.67 to yield 6.565 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 1/32 to yield 6.53 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to four basis point from two basis points at Friday's close.

Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday and Friday following a rally which saw the Canadian 30-year benchmark bond on Thursday trade with a record-low yield of 6.472 percent. Since then Canadian bonds have given back gains as investors sold to lock in profits.
The Canadian market, like its U.S. counterpart, is now focused on tomorrow's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"Everyone expects Greenspan to say nothing nice about the market. It's going to put some rain on the parade," said Dong. "To me it looks like the market wants to take a breather."

The Canadian bond market is also looking ahead to the introduction on Wednesday of new 30-year Government of Canada bond supply. The Bank of Canada on Wednesday will auction C$1.3 billion of 8.0 percent bonds due June 1, 2027.

In corporate borrowing news, TrizecHahn Corp said it will issue C$250 million of unsecured five-year debentures in Canada on a bought deal basis to refinance existing debt on the company's Place Ville Marie office complex in Montreal.
TrizecHahn said the debentures will carry a fixed interest rate which will be 70 basis points over the Government of Canada yield curve when the coupon is set later this week.

In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.11 to C$109.10 to yield 6.01 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.25 percent. The negative spread was 24 basis points, unchanged from Friday's close.
